title: DOMContentLoaded bootstrap passes its Event into initBrowser's env parameter, silently disabling the saver on the readyState 'loading' path
detail: addEventListener callbacks receive the event as first argument; env=event is truthy, event.document is undefined, so the !body guard returns and nothing wires. Any classic (non-deferred) script executes during parse with readyState 'loading'. Tests only call _initBrowser(env) directly, so this path is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Wrap the listener: root.document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initBrowser(); }); so no event object reaches the env parameter.

title: Migration header still claims erasure 'removes the row' and token 'minted lazily' — both reversed by the round-2 tombstone and mint-at-save
evidence:
+--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
+--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.
...vs same file...
+  -- Erasure tombstone: a confirmed Art. 17 deletion wipes fields/token but
+  -- keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close so a still-open form
...and...
+-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
+-- the first "email me a link" request).
...vs spec in same diff...
+  W1: tokens mint at SAVE time (upsert arg 4, COALESCE keeps existing) —
detail: The file's own erased_at comment keeps the (vacancy,email) row as a suppression tombstone, and the spec's Perkins changelog records mint-at-save; the header bullets (and 'most rows have NULL') describe pre-round-2 behaviour, misstating the schema contract.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the two header bullets: erasure wipes fields/token but keeps the keyed tombstone until vacancy close; continue_token is minted at save via COALESCE, so most rows are non-NULL.
